findings.evidence: 24/24 fresh preparations delivered the declared scope; all source hashes and complete bodies verified.
All 72 offline treatments passed independent source/passthrough fidelity reconstruction; application/security regressions and installed transports passed. Native task correctness remains unmeasured.
Fixed-width boundaries replace quadratic suffix rescanning; compatibility cases and a bounded 500,000-character subprocess regression pass. No model speedup is claimed.
C delivered source on one of 12 tasks in both repeats, but delivered the wrong type-only file; declared target scope was complete on zero tasks. V1 also delivered zero target scopes.
C mean 2.098610s versus B 1.216337s and V1 1.357629s. These are cold local components, not full coding-task times.
Mean parent CPU C 1.193451s vs B 0.720920s; separate waited-child CPU C 0.759263s vs B 0.340620s. Counters have different scopes and are not an exact total.

18/18 synthetic Python selections/fidelity passed. C preparation medians exceeded V1 at both sizes; whole-process SELF RSS was similar/slightly higher. No real-repository or TS-worker peak-memory result exists.

findings.evidence: Offline eligibility failed, so all 72 planned native assignments remain unrun. No invented token or dollar measurements.
No new memory injection; existing explicit memory features and installed memory smoke remain available.

limitations: Twelve controlled mutation tasks across four complete small upstream snapshots, six Python/six TypeScript; not a random sample or proof about larger repositories. Two repeats are not 24 independent tasks.

Expected paths are an independent author-declared repair-scope proxy. Scope coverage is not semantic dependency completeness, native correctness, or an assessment that an agent cannot solve the original task after fallback.
Known-path B is an oracle baseline: manual source discovery effort is unmeasured and excluded. No invented avoided work is credited to C.

Caches and shared-host scheduling are uncontrolled. Balanced execution order does not establish equivalent provider or OS cache state. Cold setup/preparation excludes fixture/worktree creation, imports, independent reconstruction and grading.

The local profile uses synthetic Python only. SELF RSS includes interpreter, imports, fixture/index/setup/preparation; child peak is a separate maximum, not simultaneous total or incremental preparation allocation. TS parser peak RSS was not measured.

The offline runner seals its source manifest before dispatch but has no per-observation/end-of-offline source guard. Operator sequencing and the frozen Git snapshot support this run; they are not an independently timestamped proof of runtime immutability.
Posthoc ranks and cause analyses were inspected only after the fixed gate failed. These tasks are now exposed and must not be reused as independent confirmation for a changed policy.

Actual billing, native model telemetry, cost per successful coding task and end-to-end coding latency are unavailable because native execution was not initiated. Historical API-equivalent savings are not transferred to this policy.

Tasks share only four repository snapshots and often one repair file; task-cluster bootstrap does not capture all repository correlation. Repeat two was slower in all three arms, consistent with uncontrolled timing drift; exact causes are unknown.
